transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, things at work have been just a little bit bumpy lately. I work at a meat processing plant—which is a good job, I'm really grateful to have it! 

But, um, I've been having this silly issue where I'll start doing the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or my end-of-line paperwork, and... I don't know, I somehow just leave out the very last parts? It's really embarrassing to admit, because I know my job completely depends on finishing them correctly, and I really am trying my absolute best to get it right. I just keep messing up those final steps. Is that... does that make sense for why I'd come see you? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
When you're doing those tasks at work, do you ever feel like you have to do them a certain way or repeat parts of them because you're worried something bad might happen if you don't?

Oh, um, no, not really. I hope that's okay? Like, I don't feel scared or worried that something bad will happen, and I definitely don't repeat the steps. It's actually kind of the opposite, I guess? 

I just... I honestly just sort of blank on the very last part. Or my brain just moves on to the next thing before I'm actually finished, and I don't even realize I missed it until someone points it out later. I'm not doing it on purpose or out of fear or anything like that. Does that make sense? I'm sorry if that wasn't the answer you were looking for!
Outside of work, do you find yourself forgetting to finish tasks or losing track of what you were doing, like maybe missing the last steps of something you're doing at home?

Um, at home? I... I don't think so? I mean, I feel like I'm pretty good about keeping things together at my apartment. At least, I try really hard to! 

I guess sometimes I might, you know, leave a cabinet door open or maybe forget to put the lid back on the toothpaste, but that's just normal stuff, right? Everyone does that sometimes. I don't think it's anything major like what happens at work. I usually get my chores done... eventually. Is it okay if I don't have a good example for that? I really hope I'm being helpful.
Have you ever had thoughts that bother you, like something bad might happen, and you feel like you have to do something specific or ritualistic to prevent it, even if you don’t want to?

Oh, no... no, I definitely don't have anything like that. I don't really get scary thoughts where I feel forced to do a ritual or anything. 

Um... I'm so sorry, I feel like I keep saying no to your questions! I really hope I'm not making this difficult for you, or, you know, giving you the wrong answers. It's just that my brain sort of wanders off, but it's never because I'm trying to prevent something bad. Is it... is it okay that I don't experience that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Have you noticed any recurring thoughts, images, or urges that bother you, even if they don’t lead to any specific actions?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I have anything like that. I mean, my mind definitely wanders a lot, like I was saying, but it's more just... getting distracted by random things, not like, bad or bothersome thoughts or urges. 

I'm really sorry, I know that's another "no." I hope I'm not being a frustrating patient! I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly. Is it normal that I don't have those kinds of thoughts? I really appreciate you taking the time to ask me all this, I just hope I'm actually giving you what you need to figure things out.
Outside of work, do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks or activities, like reading something or watching a show, without getting distracted?

Um, outside of work? Well, I guess... I mean, yeah, I do get distracted sometimes, but I think everyone does, right? Like, if a show is a little slow, it's normal to look at your phone. I really try to pay attention, though! 

Actually, um, where I really notice it being a problem is back at work, if that's okay to talk about? I know you asked about outside of work, I'm sorry. It's just... even when I start my shift trying *really* hard to stay locked in—like, I promise myself I'm going to focus—after a while, the cutting, the weighing, checking all the labels... it all just kind of blurs together. And then I'll realize I've just been staring at the same tray of meat or the log sheet for who knows how long, without actually taking in what I'm supposed to do next. 

I feel so bad when it happens because I really want to do a good job. Is it... is it helpful that I brought up work again? I hope I answered your question okay!
Outside of work, do you ever catch yourself zoning out or losing focus during activities that require sustained attention, like conversations, reading, or even driving?

Um, well... I guess I try really hard not to let that happen, especially with important things. Like driving, I'm always super careful, I promise! I wouldn't want to be unsafe or anything. 

But, um... maybe sometimes with reading? Or if a conversation goes on for a really long time and I don't want to be rude by interrupting... I might sort of drift a little bit. But I always try to nod and smile so the other person knows I'm still listening! I really don't want to make anyone feel bad. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of example you were looking for. I'm trying to be as helpful as I can!
When you were a child, did you ever have trouble staying focused on tasks or activities, like schoolwork or chores, or did people often tell you that you were easily distracted?

Um, as a kid? Well... I was always a really good kid, I promise! I never got into trouble or anything like that. I actually really liked school and I always tried my best to be a good student. 

But, um... I guess maybe there were some little things? Like, my mom actually still has some of my old report cards from around fourth grade. And, um, the teachers would always say really nice things, like that I was bright! But... they also usually put a note saying I needed, like, constant reminders to finish my classwork or remember to turn in my homework. 

I don't really know why that happened, because I remember understanding the lessons fine! It wasn't that I wasn't trying. It's just... I would somehow miss chunks of the instructions unless the teacher was, like, standing right by my desk. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student! I really did care about doing well. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Do you ever find it hard to stay focused during social events or personal activities, like hanging out with friends or organizing something in your personal life, and does it ever cause problems for you?

Um, social events? Oh, I really love my friends, I do! Hanging out with them is great. I always try to be a good friend and be there for them. 

I guess... well, maybe sometimes if we're in a big group or there's a lot going on, like at a party, I might kind of... drift a little bit? Like, someone will be telling a story and I really am trying to listen, I promise! But then I'll realize I missed the punchline or I don't know what they just asked me. I always feel awful when that happens, so I usually just kind of laugh and agree with whatever everyone else is doing so I don't ruin the mood. 

As for organizing things... I mean, I try my best! I wouldn't say it causes huge problems. Maybe I'm just a little messy sometimes, like anyone else? I try to keep my apartment nice, especially if people are coming over. I really don't want anyone to think I'm a slob. 

Did I answer that okay? I hope I'm not making it sound like I don't care about my friends, because I really do!
Outside of work, do you find it difficult to stay focused on organizing tasks or personal responsibilities, like managing your schedule or keeping track of your belongings?

Um... keeping track of my belongings? Well, I try my absolute best to keep everything where it belongs, I really do! I'd hate to be a burden on anyone by losing important things. 

But, um... I guess I do struggle with that a little bit. Actually, is it okay if I give an example from my job? I know you asked about outside of work, but it happens there a lot and I just feel so embarrassed about it. I work in meat processing, and... well, I'm constantly losing things I need right there on the floor. Like my cut glove, or my marker, my badge, even my safety glasses! 

It's so silly, and I always feel awful about it, because I'll swear I just had them right in my hand a second ago. And then I have to spend, like, ten minutes just retracing my steps to find them. I always try to be really quick about it so I don't bother my coworkers or slow anyone down, I promise! 

Does that... does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I brought up work for that one. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the best examples I can!
